checker_history.note: corrected contract shipped 2026-11-10 without touching any vendored byte. The vendored `LetterFrequencyChecker.build_description` replaces a `letter` kwarg outside a-z with `random.choice(string.ascii_letters)`, so the two pinned cells whose ask is punctuation (`ifeval-1122` = '#', `ifeval-1129` = '!') were decided by a coin flip under `pub-ifeval-v1` (measured strict pass 4/12 and 7/12 over 12 draws of byte-identical shipped answers). v2 restores the pinned literal character on the built instruction and counts it as-is; it re-asserts the five SHA-1/16 vendored pins above on every run and refuses to score if they move, pins determinism (20 identical draws per affected cell), and fails closed if v1 and v2 differ on more than those 2 cells. All five published IFEval arms were rescored from the shipped answer bytes (three independent scorer passes each); the per-arm corrections, the recomputed paired tests and the residual langdetect band are in IFEVAL-RESULT.md. The published `pub-ifeval-v1` rows and verdict files stay published unchanged.

livecodebench.checker_gates: self-test 18/18: pickler decodes pure data, pickler REFUSES a payload that references a global class (control payload), reference solution passes, wrong completion fails, crash fails, infinite loop -> TLE loss, empty answer fails, payload-pin mismatch fails closed as UNSCORED, over-byte-cap test is a loss not a skip; functional driver: reference passes, wrong fails, exception anatomy named, bare-method completion shims onto the stub name, float 1e-6 tolerance inside and outside, malformed case bytes UNSCORED never guessed, per-case 20 s TLE, unimported typing names rescued by one prelude retry adopted only on strict improvement; every shipped functional case (2367) decodes under the argument parser

execution_budget_pre_registered.note: caps set above the measured maxima so no question is excluded by construction; over-cap is a REJECT (a loss), never a silent skip

hidden_payload.note: the hidden tests are base64 -> zlib -> pickle -> JSON; the decoder refuses every pickle global (measured: all 175 rows decode as pure data). The tracked tasks file carries, per question, the public tests plus hidden_count and the SHA-256/16 of the canonical hidden-test JSON, and `score` fail-closes if a sidecar row does not match that pin. Publishing this payload as a GitHub release asset is a separate owner decision; until then the payload lives only on the local box and an outside reader can verify the per-question pins but not re-run the hidden battery.
